title: Finite-free scalar extension commutes with completion and its unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $a:R\to S$ a map of sheaves of commutative rings. Assume $S$ is finite free as an $R$-module sheaf, meaning $S\cong R^{\oplus d}$ for some finite $d$. Use the module derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $C(M)=M\otimes_R^L S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and the canonical Koszul completion reflectors with their units [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector]. Let $t$ be a global section of $R$, let $v$ be a global section of $S$, and suppose $a(t)=wv^e$ with $w$ a global unit of $S$ and $e\geq1$. Write $\Lambda_{R,t}$ and $\Lambda_{S,v}$ for these reflectors, with units $\eta^R,\eta^S$.

There is a canonical natural isomorphism in $D(S)$
$$\kappa_M:C\Lambda_{R,t}M\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{S,v}CM,\qquad \kappa_M\,C(\eta^R_M)=\eta^S_{CM}.$$
In particular $C$ carries locally derived $t$-complete objects to locally derived $v$-complete objects. The isomorphism is independent of a basis. It commutes with the canonical cochain shifts. For the identity coefficient map and $v=t$ it is the tensor-unit comparison. For a tower of finite-free ring-sheaf maps for which each preceding parameter is a unit times a positive power of the next, successive $\kappa$'s agree with the direct $\kappa$ under balanced derived tensor associativity.

proof.text: Put $s=a(t)$. For a complex $P$ representing $M$, form the strict augmented tower $X_m=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R[R\xrightarrow{t^m}R])$, with degrees $[-1,0]$ in the second factor and transition $(t,1)$. The finite-free strict-tower theorem says that scalar tensor is exact; hence $C$ is computed termwise on any $P$, not just on a resolution. Each Koszul tensor is the two-copy total complex (a shifted cone), so it preserves quasi-isomorphisms in $P$. The elementary balanced tensor map $(x\otimes r)\otimes z\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a(r)z$, with its inverse, identifies $C^{\operatorname{Tow}}X$ with $Y_m=\operatorname{Tot}((P\otimes_RS)\otimes_S[S\xrightarrow{s^m}S])$. It intertwines differentials because $a(t^m)=s^m$, transitions because $a(t)=s$, and degree-zero augmentations because $a(1)=1$. These are maps of entire augmented towers, natural in $P$. The two-copy formula and exact scalar tensor show that these calculations descend to $D(R)$ and $D(S)$.

proof.text: Apply the strict-tower comparison $\lambda_X:C R\lim_R X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim_S C^{\operatorname{Tow}}X$ and the tower identification in step 1. The Koszul reflector statement identifies the two limits with $C\Lambda_{R,t}M$ and $\Lambda_{S,s}CM$. We obtain a natural isomorphism $\kappa^s_M:C\Lambda_{R,t}M\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{S,s}CM$. The augmented-tower clause of the transport theorem, applied to the degree-zero maps $P\to X_m$, gives the actual equality $\kappa^s_M C(\eta^R_M)=\eta^{S,s}_{CM}$. This uses the specified total derived inverse limit, including its augmentation, rather than a choice of cones in the triangulated category. The comparison is independent of the finite-free basis by that same theorem.

proof.text: Use the Cech--Koszul dual-limit comparison for the singleton parameters $s$ and $v$ over $S$. It identifies their Koszul reflectors, with their actual units, with $R\mathcal Hom_S([S\to S[1/s]],-)$ and $R\mathcal Hom_S([S\to S[1/v]],-)$. The unit-power completeness lemma applies since $s=wv^e$, $w$ is invertible and $e\geq1$. It gives a natural isomorphism $h:\Lambda_{S,s}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{S,v}$ satisfying $h_N\eta^{S,s}_N=\eta^{S,v}_N$. Concretely its augmented localization identification fixes $S$; in $S[1/s]$, $v^{-1}=wv^{e-1}/s$, and in $S[1/v]$, $s^{-1}=w^{-1}v^{-e}$, giving inverse maps on sheafified localizations. Define $\kappa_M=h_{CM}\kappa^s_M$. Then $\kappa$ is a natural isomorphism and $\kappa_M C(\eta^R_M)=\eta^S_{CM}$. No regularity, Noetherian condition or exactness of sheaf products was used.

proof.text: If $M$ is locally derived $t$-complete, the reflector theorem makes $\eta^R_M$ invertible. The equality just proved makes $\eta^S_{CM}$ invertible, so the same theorem over $S$ shows that $CM$ is locally derived $v$-complete. For later use, for every locally derived $v$-complete $L$, precomposition with $C(\eta^R_M)$ is bijective on maps $C\Lambda_{R,t}M\to L$: indeed $C(\eta^R_M)=\kappa_M^{-1}\eta^S_{CM}$, and precomposition with $\eta^S_{CM}$ is bijective by the reflector theorem. Thus any two arrows to such $L$ agreeing after $C(\eta^R_M)$ are equal. This proves uniqueness of a unit-normalized comparison, and, independently of the construction in step 2, shows basis independence and independence of any presentation of the unit-power relation.

proof.text:
Write $c:C(N[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(CN)[1]$, $r:\Lambda_R(N[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(\Lambda_RN)[1]$, and $q:\Lambda_S(N[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(\Lambda_SN)[1]$ for the canonical cochain shift comparisons. Exact derived scalar extension supplies $c$, and the complete-triangulated theorem supplies $r,q$ with shift-compatible units. The desired equation is
$$\kappa_M[1]\,c_{\Lambda_R M}\,C(r_M)=q_{CM}\,\Lambda_S(c_M)\,\kappa_{M[1]}.$$
Precompose both sides with $C(\eta^R_{M[1]})$. Shift compatibility of $\eta^R$, naturality of $c$, and the unit equation for $\kappa_M$ reduce the left side to $\eta^S_{CM}[1]\,c_M$. The unit equation for $\kappa_{M[1]}$, naturality of $\eta^S$ along $c_M$, and shift compatibility of $\eta^S$ reduce the right side to the same expression. The common target $(\Lambda_S CM)[1]$ is complete by the complete-triangulated theorem. Step 4 cancels the precomposition. Iteration, including inverse shifts, gives every integer shift.

proof.text: For the identity coefficient map and $v=t$, let $u_N:CN\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ be the multiplication unitor, computed by $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$ in each cochain degree. The tensor-unit comparison from $C\Lambda_R M$ to $\Lambda_R CM$ is $\Lambda_R(u_M^{-1})u_{\Lambda_R M}$. Its composite with $C(\eta^R_M)$ is $\Lambda_R(u_M^{-1})\eta^R_M u_M=\eta^R_{CM}$ by naturality of the unitor and the completion unit. Its target is complete. Step 4 therefore identifies it with $\kappa_M$. This proves the stated normalization with the actual tensor unit.

source.place: Tags 099B (lemma-derived-completion) and 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul); agent assembly of finite-free scalar transport and reflector uniqueness.

proof.text:
Consider $R\xrightarrow a S\xrightarrow b T$, parameters $t,v,z$, $a(t)=wv^e$, $b(v)=uz^f$. Then $ba(t)=b(w)u^e z^{ef}$, with a unit coefficient and $ef\geq1$. Choosing bases only to verify the hypothesis gives $T\cong S^{\oplus j}\cong R^{\oplus dj}$, so the preceding construction also applies directly to $ba$. Write $\alpha:C_bC_a\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{ba}$ for balanced tensor associativity. Since all three scalar functors are exact termwise, its formula on any complex is $(x\otimes s)\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes b(s)y$, with inverse $x\otimes y\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes y$; it is natural on complexes and hence on derived categories. Compare the two arrows
$$A=\Lambda_T(\alpha_M)\,\kappa_{b,C_aM}\,C_b(\kappa_{a,M}),\qquad B=\kappa_{ba,M}\,\alpha_{\Lambda_RM}.$$
After precomposing with $C_bC_a(\eta^R_M)$, the two unit equations and naturality of $\eta^T$ give $A\,C_bC_a(\eta^R_M)=\eta^T_{C_{ba}M}\alpha_M$. Naturality of $\alpha$ and the direct unit equation give exactly the same formula for $B$. The map $C_bC_a(\eta^R_M)$, transported by $\alpha$, is $C_{ba}(\eta^R_M)$; step 4 for $ba$ makes precomposition with it injective into the complete target $\Lambda_TC_{ba}M$. Hence $A=B$. Induction on the length of a finite tower, with the explicit associative balanced-tensor formula, proves the asserted agreement for successive extensions.

No new nodes and no statement change.

I read every cited statement in full and checked each use. Step 1: exact termwise ⊗S; the balanced map to the S-Koszul tower for s=a(t) commutes with differentials, transitions and augmentations. Step 2: λ_X and its augmented-tower clause give κ^s with κ^s C(η^R)=η^{S,s}; the reflector and transport nodes use the same L_R. Step 3: Čech–Koszul θ for s and v plus unit-power completeness (s=wv^e, w a unit, e≥1) give a unit-carrying h; the localization inverses check. Step 4: the iff criterion and the Hom bijection give preservation of complete objects and cancellation of C(η^R). Steps 5–7: I composed out the shift square, the identity unitor case and the tower case A vs B after precomposition; all reduce to the same unit expressions; ba(t)=b(w)u^e z^{ef}; T≅R^{dj}. Edge cases checked: d=0, t=v=0, units, zero divisors, e=1. Closure over snapshot+side-live (690 nodes) has no cycle. The narrower injective/exact-product exchange nodes and the koszul-completion-scalar-comparison node are not duplicates.
